title: operator-notary-change-bundles-playbook
content:
Summary:
This is an early draft playbook describing the proposed Operator Notary Change Bundle (ONCB) model for customer-managed networking handoffs in Private deployments. The ONCB is a signed, time-bound artifact containing the change intent, verification metadata, and minimal runtime proof that can be recorded in the centralized audit store and provided to customers as provenance during handover.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Private customers require strong, inspectable evidence that a requested network/config change was approved, executed, and observed.
- Current approval gates produce signals scattered across systems (ticket comments, e-mails, kube events, SSH session logs) with no canonical, machine-readable package to ship to customers or to use for automated rollback/on-call decisions.
- For regulated customers the auditor workflow requires an end-to-end bundle: who approved, what was applied, what validation passed, and cryptographic proof that the operator who performed the change was authorized at that time.

Goals (short):
- Define a compact, signed Change Bundle schema that is easy to generate by operator tooling and verifiable by the control plane and customer tools.
- Add minimal friction to operator workflows (keep UX similar to existing change commands).
- Surface change provenance in the audit-log UX and make it exportable to customers.
- Support automatic rollback triggers when bundle verification fails for post-change probes (latency, connectivity, attestation).

Non-goals:
- This doc does not specify the entire KMS/HSM integration policy (separate security PRD).
- Not a full spec for attestations from third-party network appliances (we define a minimal ingestion contract).

Actors:
- Operator: person executing the change using the operator CLI or console.
- Approver: person or automated system that grants authorization (could be a delegated policy engine).
- Notary service: Redwood service that signs and timestamps bundles using the operator-specific key (or escrowed key in enterprise installs).
- Control plane audit-store: canonical repository for bundles and derived events.
- Customer verifiers: scripts or UI that validate incoming bundles during handoff.

High-level flow:
1) Operator opens change ticket (JIRA-OPS-xxxx) and requests approval following existing gating rules.
2) Approver approves in ticket; approval triggers a short-lived authorization token (scope: change-id, expiry: t+15m) from the delegation service.
3) Operator runs 'rwd change apply --bundle <change-id>' which:
   - collects change manifest (affected resources, diffs), pre-change probes (connectivity pings, baseline metrics), and the authorization token metadata,
   - creates a compressed bundle (format: gzipped JSONL) annotated with provenance fields,
   - uploads bundle to the Notary service which affixes a signature and authoritative timestamp, returns notary-id.
4) Operator applies change; operator agent streams runtime events back to control-plane (kube events, task exit statuses, quick probes).
5) Post-change probes run (customer-defined smoke tests); results are attached to the bundle and re-signed or appended as a linked attestation object.
6) Final bundle is stored in the audit-store and surfaced to both Redwood Console and the customer's handover page.

Bundle content (recommended minimum fields):
- change_id: string (ticket id or UUID)
- operator_id: string (SAML/scoped username)
- approver_id: string
- auth_token_id: string
- requested_at: ISO8601
- started_at: ISO8601
- finished_at: ISO8601 (optional if change failed midstream)
- resources_changed: list-of-strings (paths / resource ids)
- diff_summary: short text (single paragraph)
- pre_change_probe_summary: short text
- post_change_probe_summary: short text
- notary_signature: base64 string (signature over canonical bundle)
- notary_id: string
- notary_timestamp: ISO8601
- observability_markers: list-of-strings (trace ids, span ids)
- forensic_markers: list-of-strings (e.g., SSH session id, bastion transaction id)
- operator_agent_logs_uri: https://... (short-lived presigned URL)

Note: we intentionally keep the resource lists as short strings to avoid shipping large binary artifacts inside bundles. The bundle is a manifest+pointer model.

Verification semantics (consumer side):
- Verify signature matches the registered notary_id and the notary keyset for the deployment.
- Validate token_id and approver_id: look up delegation engine (or local cache) to ensure token scope covers change_id and wasn't revoked.
- Cross-check observability_markers with control-plane traces to confirm events occurred in the time window.
- Run post-change probe assertions; if critical assertions fail, mark bundle as failed and initiate rollback policy (see next section).

Automatic rollback policy (configurable):
- Default: on critical probe failure within 10 minutes, create rollback bundle and re-run verification.
- Optional stricter policy per-customer: require 2 independent post-change probes, or require operator to acknowledge a failed bundle before rollback.

Integration points with customer-managed networking:
- Customers often prefer the notary to be exportable as a single artifact for their compliance teams. Provide an "export-handshake" endpoint that issues a customer-signed acceptance token that the customer can store alongside the bundle.
- For VPC handoffs, we capture the CIDR changes, BGP/peering descriptors, and proof that routes were propagated (bgp-announcement markers).
- Support an on-prem Notary mode where the customer's HSM retains the notary key; Redwood's notary service accepts a pre-signed stamping token from that HSM and records the bundle. (See security PRD for HSM integration.)

UX considerations (operator):
- Single command to produce and sign bundles; default flags to attach pre/post probes.
- Clear console messages when a bundle is uploaded, with notary_id and a link to the audit entry.
- Minimal blocking: if notary service is temporarily unavailable, operator can create a locally-signed bundle (operator-key) that is marked as 'provisional' and auto-reconciled when notary is reachable.

Audit-store surface and queries:
- Index by change_id, operator_id, approver_id, notary_id, resource, and timeframe.
- Filtering UX: show state (provisional | signed | failed-verification | rolled-back)
- Export formats: JSONL, PDF summary, and a compact TAR containing pointers and presigned logs.

Forensics and long-term retention:
- Bundles are compact; long-lived artifacts (logs, packets, traces) remain in their native stores with pointers in the bundle.
- For high-compliance customers we offer a retention add-on (WORM copy of signed bundles + GPG-based escrow).

Operational runbook (brief):
- If bundle fails signature verification: alert secops and mark change as suspicious; do not allow automated rollback until manual review unless policy permits.
- If observability_markers missing: attempt re-ingest, then mark bundle 'incomplete' and escalate to operator for re-run.
- If notary service down: allow provisional bundles for up to 24h then block new changes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Canonical bundle format: JSONL vs CBOR? Tradeoffs: size vs readability. (Action: eng/serving-runtime to prototype CBOR/JSONL size delta — ETA 2 weeks)
- Exact cryptographic signing model for enterprise on-prem Notary (HSM integration). Security gating required.
- How to surface partial-proofs from third-party network appliances (BGP routers, firewalls) — define ingestion API.
- UX for customers who want to require multi-approver signatures (AND / OR policy).

Appendix: quick example (human readable)
(change_id: JIRA-OPS-2345)
operator_id: aisha.menon@redwood
approver_id: mateo.chen@redwood
notary_id: notary-eu-01
notary_timestamp: 2025-01-09T16:02:11Z
resources_changed: [vpce-43a1, route-2034]
post_change_probe_summary: "bgp: announced routes to peer 10.1.2.1; tcp-connector: successful 3/3 probes; latency xfer < 20ms"
notary_signature: (base64...)

---
Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally operational and UX-forward. Looking for feedback from Eng infra (Mateo), SRE (Evan), and Security (Priya).
- If this approach is acceptable we will spin up a small spike to implement: CLI changes, notary service shim, bundle persistence schema, and Console UI mockups.
